laws.rule: Baja California charges a state lodging tax (Impuesto sobre Servicios de Hospedaje) on lodging received in the state: hotels, motels, villas, cabins, campgrounds, caravan parks, tourist marinas, timeshare, and stays booked through digital platforms. The guest is the taxpayer and the host collects it. The rate is set each year in the state revenue law: 5.0% in the 2025 law, 7.0% for motels (Ley de Hacienda del Estado de Baja California, art. 127 to 130; Ley de Ingresos del Estado 2025, art. 6). The 2026 revenue law was not read.

Baja California's alcohol law bans selling alcohol on the street, in parks and in public squares, except under a temporary permit from the municipality (Ley para la Venta, Almacenaje y Consumo Público de Bebidas Alcohólicas, art. 23). Licensed venues may not open before 10:00 or go past 03:00 the next day, and councils can cut those hours (art. 17). Venues must stop selling on dates set by federal election rules and on days a council or the governor orders for safety, and must not serve anyone under 18 (art. 26).

Baja California's smoke-free law bans smoking or keeping a tobacco product lit in 100% smoke-free spaces (enclosed public places) and in public and private schools (Ley de Protección contra la Exposición al Humo de Tabaco, art. 15). Restaurants and bars must enforce the ban inside; a venue may offer a smoking area only if it meets the law's conditions (art. 17). Tobacco can't be sold to minors or as single cigarettes (art. 15).
